utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. May we begin by taking the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours. Appearing for the prosecution today is Tom Hannis, Belinda Pidwell, and Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence. I'm sorry, and Dominic Kennedy, our intern is also present. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm now addressing the witness. Good afternoon to you, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. You, as you would be aware, have been summoned to attend as a witness before the -- this Tribunal and your evidence is being received by way of videolink. The Court Officer who is with you, as I'm sure would have been explained to you, is there to assist and facilitate the testimony which the Tribunal is receiving live by way of this videolink. Have you appeared before the Tribunal previously, or have you appeared in court in your -- anywhere in -- in your country of residence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, I would begin by explaining the procedure to you. And that is that the side calling you, in this case the Prosecution, would begin by asking you questions, after which the counsel for each of the two accused persons would have a right to ask you questions. Then the Prosecution could re-examine you, and the Chamber, itself may have questions of you. I would begin by asking you to state your name for the record, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Asim Basic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7th of February, 1951, in the village of Basici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your profession or occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a -- I am a mining engineer, and I used to operate a bagger or excavator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, I would now invite the Prosecution to begin by asking its questions of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But before she does that, I would now invite the Court Officer to have you take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes, Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Basic.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to hear me and see me?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see and hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a series of questions, and the questions that I ask will be translated as I speak, so I ask you just to pause between my questions and your answers so the interpreters can keep up with us. Mr. Basic, do you have a bundle of documents in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are some.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Well, if we just leave them in front of you for the moment, and I'll be referring to them during the course of your testimony this afternoon. Firstly I'd just like to ask you some background questions, sir. We've heard that you were born in the municipality of Gacko in southern Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And am I correct in saying that you lived there for your entire life up until the war broke out in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I lived in Gacko and worked there and was born there until the war broke out. I haven't been anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And the town that you lived in was the town of Basici, the town of your birth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: No, it is called Fazlagica Kula. It is made up of 13 villages and they constitute a local community. My own village is called Basici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If my math is correct in 1991, would you have been 40 years old. Does that sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I was born in 1951.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And, sir, are you married?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of February, 1951. Yes, I'm married. I've got a wife and four kids.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you still live in the municipality of Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: No. When I was evicted from Gacko, I didn't return, because I didn't dare. Now I'm in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Tribunal the -- the municipalities that surround the municipality of Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Gacko is surrounded by the municipalities of Nevesinje, on the north; a village on Trebinje on the south; then Foca on one side ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And is the terrain of the municipality generally flat, or is it mountainous?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The Gacko Polje, that is the Gacko field is flat but there are mountains also.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And before the war, would you agree with me that approximately 11.000 people lived in this municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, round about that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And of those 11.000 people, approximately 35 per cent were from your ethnic background, Bosniaks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, if we take the entire municipality. But the town of Gacko itself was predominantly Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: That's right. Would you agree that the town of Gacko itself was approximately 51 per cent Bosniak and 49 per cent predominantly Serb and other ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There were two or three Croats, and all the rest were Serbs, and 51 per cent were Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Outside of the -- the town of Gacko, which areas in the municipality did the Bosniaks predominantly live?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Kula Fazlagica was made up of 13 villages and they were all Bosniaks and there was also Borac. These were inhabited by Bosniaks and all the other villages were Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd ask if can you look at the documents that are in the bundle in front of you and turn to tab -- the document behind tab 1. It's 65 ter 10135.23. Sorry, 101735. 10137.23. Do you have that map in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it is one of the maps that's in the binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree that this is a -- a basic map of the municipality of Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, to a great extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And that it has the -- on the map it has marked the Muslim towns that you were referring to: Fazlagica Kula at the bottom, and Borac at the top?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And your town was one of the hamlets within Fazlagica Kula; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. It there was a connection with another village in the direction of Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And besides those two villages that you've named, the other towns that we see named on that map, were they predominantly Serb towns?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Avtovac was Serbian, Ravni also, Kokorina. And Cemerno was also a Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: We see also on that map, and you've just mentioned the town of Avtovac, was there anything in particular that was based at that town?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There was a military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And just to give us a little bit of perspective, how far is that from the -- the main town of Gacko that we see there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Two and a half or 3 kilometres, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And to give us also a little bit of perspective, in your town, how many households made up your town of Basici?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There were 70 houses in Basici, and there were three persons that lived in each of these houses, three to four.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: There's also a thermal power plant in the municipality of Gacko. Are you able to show us on the map before you -- approximately where that is? Perhaps the court Registrar could assist you by providing a pen.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: It should be here. Here, between Gacko and the place in the south.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I wonder if the court Registrar in Sarajevo could assist the witness in marking the -- the map before him, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If you could just place a number 1 where the thermal power plant is, please.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm in your hands at this point whether you want the witness to hold it up to the camera or that we could simply tender it and the Registrar can bring it back. Thank you. Could I please tender that document as an exhibit at this stage then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit Number P00914. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Pidwell, do you anticipate this witness making any further markings on the copy of the map that he has?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: No, I don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And, finally, on these general background questions, sir, could you briefly describe what the relations were like between Bosniaks and Serbs in the municipality of Gacko before the war.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I don't -- I think we're having a problem. There is no translation coming through, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the war the relationships were excellent until the moment some paramilitary formations came from Serbia about a couple of months before the war. Before that, everything was excellent, we socialised, we celebrated our religious holidays together. It was good.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you some questions about what happened after the elections in 1990. Do you recall who was appointed the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Mitar Lazetic was appointed the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And from which political party was he from?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. We worked together. He was one of the engineers in the thermal electric plant.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you know who -- do you recall who was appointed the chief of the SJB in Gacko after the -- directly after the elections?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Elvedin Dzubur was the commander of the SJB and Tale Talovic was the chief of the SUP, until the moment the SDS took over. After that, a certain person was brought over from Foca and appointed commander of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the -- sorry. The -- after the elections was the chief of the SJB appointed from the SDS or from the SDA; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I believe that he was from the SDS. And before that, he was from the SDA. After the elections the person from the SDA was the chief of public security, and then the SDS came and forcefully removed that person from office.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the chief of public security from the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Tale Talovic. And the police commander was Elvedin Dzubur.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you've said that these positions were then taken over by the SDS. Do you recall how that happened?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: When the paramilitary formations arrived in Gacko, there was a rebellion, and then they forcibly removed both the police commander and the police chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know who was appointed in their place?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: A certain name called Popovic was brought to that position and the police commander was Vitomir Popic, a former police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm going ask you to repeat the name of the police commander because I'm not sure it was caught by the interpreters. Could you name the police commander?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The police commander was Vitomir Popovic, and the chief I don't know what his first name was. I know that his family name was Popovic and the other was Vitomir Popic. And I don't know Popovic's first name. I only know that his family name was Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: The -- the police commander Popovic, did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I knew him -- I knew 99 per cent of the children in Gacko let alone the police commander. Of course I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did you know Popic personally?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I knew Popic personally. And as for Popovic, I did not know him, and I never saw him before.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, I just need to go back a little bit. These names are a little bit confusing because they are so similar. The -- there are two gentlemen who are the police chief and the police commander of the SJB in Gacko. The one that you have said you knew was -- just to clarify, was Popic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, Popic. And the other one was Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you have said that -- initially you said that Popovic, that you knew Popovic, but can you confirm whether you knew [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know Popovic; no, I didn't. What I am saying is that I knew Popic. I didn't know Popovic. Popovic was brought to our village from Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at a document, please. It's under tab 10 in your binder, and it's 65 ter 2133.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Popovic ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you have that page in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Going through the names from the top, can you -- will you see that under number one it says Vojin Popovic. Is that the name -- is that the person that you were referring to that you did not --

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Vojin Popovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And underneath.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Vitomir Popic. That's the person whom I didn't know personally. Vitomir Popic. I knew him. Because he used to work as a police officer in Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And going down the list, sir, are there any other names on that list that you recognise as people that you know personally or knew personally?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Mladen Vukovic, Milivoj Vukovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is reading names.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have the interpretation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew all those who are on the list. I knew them by sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And after Popovic was appointed, did you ever encounter him in the town of Gacko, in his role as the chief of police?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, in passing. I happened to see him oftentimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be admitted and marked at this juncture, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit Number P00915. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I think -- Ms. Pidwell, I think we should clarify something in the -- in the transcript. At page 10, line 22 -- no, no, no. Because there is a confusion about who the witness knows and who he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew them all by sight. I knew 95 per cent of the children and everybody. I knew them all by sight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Except Popovic. I can't -- I can't find -- I can't find it in the transcript anymore. But at a certain moment he says -- well, in the transcript he seems to say, Popic, I don't know him. But the -- the Vitomir Popic was your question and not his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew Popic well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Would Your Honours like me to clarify that once more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No, no. As long as it is clear in the transcript and there is no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, can you explain how it is that you say that you knew the majority of the people in Gacko but you didn't know Popovic before his appointment?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Popovic had lived in Foca. I didn't know him. After the elections, he was brought over from Foca to be what he was to be. He had not lived in Gacko before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Sir, we've just talked about how the -- the SDS appointed these two men into these positions. Are you able to -- do you know if there were any other Bosniaks who were replaced by Serbs in the municipality of Gacko during -- in the pre-war period?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They replaced Asim Faglagic [phoen], who was a doctor in the hospital. Izet Skoplj [phoen] in the school, in the primary school, and there you go.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall the first time that -- when you saw armed forces passing through Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: That's all right. Can you describe what you saw and what you remember?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I remember that I saw them passing and I -- and a relative of mine were counting them. 350 tanks, and other vehicles went in the direction of Mostar and further on towards Dubrovnik, and the rest remained stationed on the hilltops around Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And do you recall the general reaction of the Bosniaks in your community to this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Bosniaks considered them an occupation army; whereas, the Serbs praised them and threw flowers on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And can you describe if and how tensions between the two ethnicities developed after this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: For a while, we continued working together without any problems, until the moment some paramilitary formations came from Serbia. They were billeted in the hotel and then the went around the Serb villages and trained the Serb youth. And that's how it all started. And then Armin Boskovic and Nermin Grebovic-- or rather Zoran Grebovic were killed. And that's when tensions actually started.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Where were they killed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They were killed as they were driving potatoes to Sarajevo. On the way back, they were killed in a place called Cember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: If you can have a look once again, sir, at the map that you were looking at before under tab 1, is the place that you described as Cember on that map?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Cember is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And how far is that from the town of Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: About 15 to 20 kilometres, between 15 and 20 kilometres. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did the Bosniak community do after these two men were killed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There was a protest rally in the centre of Gacko. There were Serbs who joined them as well and participated in that protest rally.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did the Serb authorities take any steps as a result of that protest?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They promised but they didn't deliver. They knew who had killed them, but they did not take any steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions now, sir, about events which took place in April and May of 1992. Did -- did Bosniak or Muslim businesses continue to operate during this time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about events which took place after -- or during and after April 1992. And, in particular, whether Bosniak businesses continued to operate or if anything happened to them.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: All the shops were torched or blown up, and people could not work anymore. Everything was over.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Did you continue going to work?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I personally continued going to work, but those who worked in town, to be honest, well, they did not go, or stopped going regularly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And your place of work was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, is the witness having some difficulty? I don't know if the Court Officer is responding to my question. But I can't hear her.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I think she is but we can't hear her, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter believes that the witness asked the Court Officer for a piece of paper and a pen to make notes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] No, I apologise, Your Honours. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if that with a system in his testimony, we have no objection. She seems to be saying that that's not what --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Can -- can you hear me at all, Your Honours? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It appears that there's a technical problem and we're going to have to rise until this is resolved. I don't know if it is possible to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. I understand it should be resolved in five or ten minutes. --- Break taken at 3.10 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] We can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please, please go ahead. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, before we left off -- addressing with regards to witness's request to look at a piece of paper that he has in his pocket to remind his ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only because I have some dates on that piece of paper and they are relevant for my testimony. They will help jog my memory about the dates, that piece of paper that I have. And that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do counsel have a view on this? My -- I would have -- in terms of the practice and jurisprudence of the Tribunal, the -- my own experience, of course, is that the -- a witness can -- if he has a document that he made himself, that he can use it to refresh his memory but the other side has a right to inspect it which is a practical problem in this regard. Do counsel have a view on this, particularly the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: We object to this, Your Honour. He is called viva voce. A contemporaneous document made at times of the events is one thing, but we see no basis for having this witness jot down notes if he is testifying viva voce. He is testifying from personal experience apparently, so he shouldn't need this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And that's probably standard. But, of course, we all remember the overriding rule that testimony is not an exercise in -- in memory is an exercise in truth-telling, and unless there is a -- particularly having regard to the length of time that would have elapsed, if the witness -- I suppose questions could be asked as to the source of the notes that he would have made, but the -- if before he came into court he would have made notes to assist him -- his own notes to assist him in terms of dates, I -- I would be inclined to allow him to refer to them, provided, of course, he explains that they were his own notes that he was just replicating. Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm happy to ask him numerous questions about the note. And perhaps it could be MFI'd and brought back for the Defence to see it at the conclusion of his testimony or tendered so it could form part of the record if Your Honours are happy for him to refer to it. I can ask him certainly when he made those notes and from what source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, if he is permitted to use them I think it is inevitable and unavoidable that they would have to be -- if not exhibited certainly brought to the attention of the Defence for their examination before they -- so that they can by some means or other ask questions based on -- to test the authenticity of -- of those notes and accuracy of those notes. But the foundation question is that the Chamber must be satisfied that they are the witness's own notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'll lead him through those questions with Your Honours' leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Mr. Basic, you have referred to some -- a piece of paper that you have with you, or the Registrar has now. Could you please, firstly, tell the Tribunal when you -- you made the notes that are contained on that paper?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I made those notes a long time ago. They were in my pocket. A long time ago, I made notes of the dates and the events. And that's all. If the dates are very important, I can look them up on that piece of paper. If the dates are not at all important, then I can't be bothered. I don't even have to look at the paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: When you say "a long time ago," sir, can you be a little bit more precise with when that was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I really wouldn't be able to tell you. I don't know what happened yesterday let alone about that paper, when I made those notes. As things evolved and as things happened, I made notes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And, sir, is that the note made from your own memory or from another source?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They are based on my own memory. Because I also had a notebook where I recorded all the dates and events. They were like my diaries, momento books.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the circumstances, I ask that he be able to use that note to refresh his memory on the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Chamber rules that the witness may be permitted to use the document in question, as a means of refreshing his memory. The -- we would have to devise a practical means to allow the Defence to exercise its right to examine the document and ask questions on it. Sorry, if that means tendering it formally which is unusual for refreshing memory documents that may be the route.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, you are able to use that piece of paper to assist you with the dates, if -- but when you do so, we will -- we will note down that are you using that document. And at the end of your testimony, if you could give that to the Registrar, we will formally put it in the court record. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, will we get this document before cross-examination? Which I believe is what you are indicating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Chamber would welcome assistance from counsel as to what I call the practical means of putting the Defence in the position to ask such questions as it is entitled to ask about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, there are scanners and e-mail, there's fax. That's two viable options.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: We will endeavour ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I -- I am advised by the Registry that one possible means is that the Court Officer may send it to the Tribunal by fax during the next break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall when you stopped going to work in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether you continued with your work throughout the course of the year, or did you stop at some stage?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I stopped at some stage, and I no longer worked at -- I stayed at home because people were being arrested, and I didn't go to work after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall an incident at work which made you decide not to return?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I remember that I was late for work once, and my supervisor said to me that three armed reserve police officers had come looking for me. I knew one of -- he knew one of them. That man's name was Dragan Bratic [phoen] but he didn't know the two others. That's when I decided not to go to work anymore. They had come to take me -- to bring me in for an interview, but the people who were brought in for interviews were actually locked up in a basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I want to show you a photo, sir, from the booklet that you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 10254, and it's in tab 4 of the booklet.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: This is the Terma Hotel at Gacko. I know it. Of course, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you've referred to a basement in your previous answer. Was this the -- the basement of this hotel that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was a bar, so-called bar in the hotel. Actually, it wasn't just a basement ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Did you ever go into that -- that bar or basement of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there two or three times with some buddies. We went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How do you know that people were detained there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, how do I know? Everybody knew about it because people were taken there and you couldn't go without noticing, without being noticed. And later on, the wives went there to fetch their husbands.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know any people who were detained there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Certainly. I know every -- every single man in Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And what was the ethnicity of the people who were detained there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They weren't Serbia; they were Bosniaks. They were taken away from their houses, from their workplaces, from the streets. They would catch people and take them away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'd ask that that photograph be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit Number P00916. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And just to assist the Trial Chamber, sir, how far away was this hotel from the police station in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Some five -- 500 metres, less than a kilometre. And if you -- you count from the centre of Gacko, it was about a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: While we've got the booklet in front of you, I'd ask that you turn to tab 2, which is 65 ter number 10256, please.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: This is the police building in Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I ask that that be admitted and marked at this stage, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number P00917. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And if you turn to the next tab, number 3, 65 ter 10257, you'll see another photograph. This time it's taken from the air.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Just waiting for it -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It is probably not a perspective you're familiar with, but are you able to recognise any of the buildings in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I know some buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Perhaps the court Registrar can assist the witness with a pen. And if, sir, you're able to mark the buildings and name the buildings that you recognise on that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mrs. Registrar please be asked to turn off the microphone while manipulating and turning the pages. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is the police station. I can't see a staircase. Or maybe this is the police station. I can't really find my way in this photograph. I know these buildings here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, the buildings that you do know, if you could just name them, please, and mark them with a 1 and a 2, if you can tell us what you're referring to, please.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: This looks more like a grocery store to me. I have great trouble finding my way in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: That's all right, sir. We'll leave it at that. We can put the photo away now if -- if that's all right. Sir, are you able to tell us whether the SJB building in Gacko was in the centre of town or outside the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: It was almost in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Just about to move ton another topic, Your Honours. I'm not sure that we've had a break, whether we are going to take a break now or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, in as much as the break was only about five minutes, and I think for the convenience of the accused, persons who would have been in court, I prefer to -- and also the background mechanics, for want of a better word, it is better to stick to the regular time. So we will take the break now if this is a convenient point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before you continue, Ms. Pidwell, I assume that Defence counsel has in hand the faxed copy of the document the witness used to refresh his memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Pidwell.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Mr. Basic, before we took the break, we heard your evidence that you had stopped working in 1992. And could you now tell us whether you stayed in your home at Basici for the rest of the year, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't stay at home. I spent two or three months in the mountains, and then I went to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What happened -- what was the event that took place which forced you into the mountains?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The Yugoslav army drove us out with grenades. And then the police, the reserve forces and the active forces, and whoever they found they killed so we had to flee because we were unarmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Was your home affected by any bombing or shelling during this time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was at home when a shell hit my house and my house burnt to the ground. Everything was destroyed and all the entire village was affected. And then the reserve police forces and the regular police and also the local Serbs came and whatever they found, they picked up, they took with them, and everything else was burnt.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So after your home was hit by the shell, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: When the shell hit my house, my entire family was there. But there were two concrete layers so the shell couldn't pierce them. But I took my entire family, including the children, and we took to the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How did you get to the mountains?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, it isn't far. Our village was at the foot of the mountain. It was by mere chance that we weren't hit by shells, because thousands of shells landed there in those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm assuming by your answer you -- you mean that you walked to the mountains with your family?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, we walked. It isn't far, you know. It's -- it's only a -- 20 minutes walk and you're there. Our village is right next to the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And on this walk from your home to the mountains after your home had been shelled, what did you see around you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Only smoke and fire, and there was nothing else to see. Everything was ablaze, the entire village.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were there other people around at this time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There were people in the village, but everybody left the village to go to Ljut, the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers or police at this time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, later. They were reserve police officers. They wore blue uniforms. Later, we did go back to the village to look for food. And then we ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: When you say "later," do you mean later that day, or on a -- on a separate day?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: On the following day when night had fallen. But sometimes we did go there in day-time too. Because we spent two months in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when you saw the reserve police officers, were they -- where were they?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, when the army -- the Uzice Corps had deployed their guns and tanks on the hilltops around the village, once they had stopped shelling, then they would loot the villages. And what hadn't already been burned, they would burn on that occasion. And if they found anybody alive, they would kill him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "they," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I mean the army and the police. Majo Kovacevic, for example, was a reserve police officer. I saw him first. He killed two sons of a Menzuovic [phoen] in my village. And I saw him in police clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And can describe those police clothes for the Tribunal, please.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, I know the reserve police force. I was an army reservist and the police had blueish uniforms. Formally, they wore red stars, but, at that time, they wore kokardes on Sajkaca hats.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you to look at a document, please. It's 65 ter 2394. It is behind tab 8 in the documents you have in front of you. This document is a list of employees, reserve police force for April 1992 in Gacko. And I want to know if you recognise any of the names, the 75 names, that are on that list. Perhaps if you could just tell us the number, if you read through the list and recognise a name as a person that you know to have been in the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I ask that that document be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry. These are names of persons he recognise as police officers. Is something else -- just pause for a moment. Is there something else that you propose to do with this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, this is a list of the reserve police officers for Gacko, and some of the names will become apparent later on in this witness's testimony as being participants of the events that will take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit Number P00918. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, if we can go back now to the -- to your story, the event that took place when you went into the mountains. How long did you stay in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And how many other Bosniaks were living with you in the mountains during that time, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Approximately -- about 5 or 600 women, children, and adults.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, I notice the witness is producing a piece of paper. Is this the same bit of paper that we would have had earlier?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the same, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did this group of 5 or 600 stay together in the mountains, or did they break up at some stage?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: We were in groups, you know, but we all knew of each other. We knew all knew where everybody else was. We kept to our separate groups, but we knew where each group was. The mountain is huge, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you to look at a document which is under tab number 11 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 2932. Sorry, 65 ter 2649.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: This is similar to the document that the Serbs sent us, inviting us to surrender, the women, the children, and all of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when you say that the Serbs sent to you, was that while you were in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: You said that you -- the Serbs sent you this document. Did they send it to you while you were in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And how did you --

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: A woman brought it to us. She was Meho Zekic's wife. She was from the village of Crnice. That was a mixed village inhabited by Muslims and Serbs. Her husband's best man, whose name was Pasinic, had given her that letter to take us to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of what the Serbs were wanting you to do at this time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They wanted us men to surrender, and we wouldn't do that. We remained in the mountain. The women and the children went to a place called Kotlina. There were some buses there, they got on the buses, and they were taken to Perkovic-Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I ask that this document be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P00919. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So you told us that the women went to a place called Kotlina and were taken away on buses. What did you do at that -- after they'd gone?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: We remained in the mountain until the moment we heard from them that they had arrived in Stolac, and we heard that via radio connections through ham radio operators.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Who remained in the group with you? Who remained in the group with you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: After the women and children had left the mountain and surrendered and been taken away on buses, you said that you and others stayed in the mountains. You remained in a group of people. And do you recall who was in that group with you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: All of us. All of us able-bodied. What do you mean who was with us? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Can you name the people who were -- stayed with you in the group?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: All from Fazlagica Kula and [indiscernible]. Everybody between the ages of 20 and 70, everybody remained in the mountain. Over 300 of us stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Am I right in understanding there were just men?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: A few younger women. But not many; three, four, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did this group of 300 break up at some stage?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: All of us together went to Trnovo and from Trnovo we dispersed and went in the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How big was the group of you that went in the direction of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Certain groups of five to six went in the direction of Stolac. Some went across Zelengora, and the group where I was, the whole group consisted of over 250 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Did you get to -- to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Mostar and stayed there almost until the moment the war was over.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: At some stage did you encounter the -- some armed forces, the Serbian-Montenegrin army?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Not on the way there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when you encountered them and the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you, we did not encounter the Serb troops, because we took a road across mountains and we hid. We wanted to avoid being seen by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, sir, the circumstances of your arrest.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Before that group, I set off in the direction of Stolac and as I descended into Berkovici we had walked to Berkovici, we descended into Berkovici, and we were met by the Serb and Serb -- Montenegrin army. We were surrounded but them, and we surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How many of you at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There were a total of ten of us.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, how many of you were in that group at that time? The interpreter didn't quite catch your answer.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There were ten of us men and one woman.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to recall their names?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: You mean those men who were with me? Of course, I can. They were all my relatives. I am going to rank them by age. Dzafer Basic, Smajo Basic, Basic Edhem, Asim Basic, Nazif Basic, Ejub Basic, Elmir Basic, Husnija Basic, and Sutko Civic, and Muvedeta Civic, Asmajia's wife, so her married name was Basic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were any of the people that you have just named under the age of 18?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Three. Husnija, Elvir, and Sulejman. They were under 15, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: You've told us that you were with this group and you became surrounded and that you surrendered. Were you all -- did you all surrender?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The Serb line was there. They were on both sides of the road. When we walked down there, they started shooting at us and yelled that we should surrender, and so we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So what happened to you after you surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Once we surrendered, we waited for a while in front of the house where their officers were lying, and we had to wait for the changing of the shifts, and they put us on a bus and drove us to some abandoned school at Dabar which is some two kilometres away from Berkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And when you say "they," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: In your answer, you said "they put us on a bus and drove us to the school at Dabar." Who were you referring to; who put you on the bus?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Those soldiers that were holding that line who took us prisoner. And one group of them was going on home leave, and another group was arriving to replace them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Before you got to the school at Dabar, were you taken anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: First, they questioned me in the police station. There was a police officer, probably the commander, well, he was kind of fair. But, later, we were mistreated in that school.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Which police station were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: At Berkovici. And our IDs were taken away from us, and our money, whoever had money.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the school in Dabar?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: We stayed two days and two nights at the school in Dabar. Until Ramo Sudzum with his police officers came to fetch us with the -- with a small bus of that catering company driven by a man called Supic, and Radmilo came with five or six reserve police officers and took us to Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to recall the names of any of the reserve police officers who took you to Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Of course. I remember Ramo Radmilo Sudzum. He was a kind of commander of that station. There was also Slobo Todorovic and Bosko Starovic, and one police officer from Konjic; I don't know his name. He was a refugee from Konjic in Gacko and then he was a police officer in Konjic and Gacko. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did you go straight to Gacko, or was the van stopped on the way?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: We -- when we arrived at Koricka Jama they were the two brothers, Samardzic, Zeljko and Nedjo. They stopped the van and they were wearing military uniforms and they had beards and kokardes. And Ramo said to us, "Be quiet because these people are crazy, don't say a thing otherwise they will kill you," and Popic ordered us to bring them to Gacko alive because we need them. That's what he said to them. And then they let us through.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did you know who these two Samardzic brothers were?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Of course, I did. Nedjo Samardzic, and his brother Zeljko. They also had a third brother who had died earlier. They were from Slana; that's a village in the direction of Bileca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What was their reputation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: What? They ... they were shepherds. They had their livestock in the mountains. And they -- some Serb killed their brother and then the newspapers wrote about ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be made to repeat. We didn't catch the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, the interpreters didn't catch the last part of your answer. You were telling us how a Serb had killed their brother, and -- and then the newspapers wrote about it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They were sitting in a pub, they and a Serb, and they got drunk and one man got hit on his head with a bottle and died. And later on, they caught him in Bileca and cut his head off and kicked his head around Bileca. And they had been imprisoned, I don't know for how long in Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time of day it was when you arrived in Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I think it may have been around 12.00 or 1.00. At night.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And whereabouts in Gacko were you taken?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: We were taken to the police station, and we found 200 persons there, women, children, men, soldiers. Then we were driven out of the bus. And everybody was beating us, until we were locked up in that cell, in the -- in the prison of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So when you entered the police station at Gacko, did you see any police officers there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. Apart from this one man who was guarding the prison, the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So who put you in the police cell?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The ones that had brought us there, Ramo Sudzum and Slobo Todorovic and those guys. And they handed us over to the duty officer, and he locked us up in that cell inside the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How many of your group were in the cell with you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There was Smaja with me, his wife, his son, and his brother-in-law, as well as myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you know where the other members of the group were taken?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: There were two cells. The size was two metres by three. And there were those wooden cots, and we sat on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Besides the wooden cots, was there anything else in the cell?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. We found uniforms, some overcoats and jackets, and some bags that belonged to some of our acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of those acquaintances?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Of course, I do, they are my relatives. We found the jacket of Dervo Zulovic who was a police officer. His brother, Sevro [phoen] Zulovic and another, Fehim Zulovic, who was an engineer at the thermal power plant. There was Bekim Karajlo and Serif, and we found some maps in the bag and some cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: During the time that you were detained in the SJB building in Gacko, were you given any food or water?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: No way. We couldn't even step outside. We even had to relieve ourselves there. Food and water? Oh, come on. Only one policeman, Mirko Koprivica, who was a duty officer, gave us a can of -- a can of meat, some canned meat and some bread. And that was all the food that we got for five or six days.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: What happened the following morning? You arrived at the SJB building at approximately midnight. Can you tell us what happened in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: In the morning, once we heard that the employees and the police were coming, we were locked up inside, I didn't see who it was, but we heard a noise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Did someone come to your -- to your cell?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, later. Slobo Todorovic and Bosko Starovic and Vlatko Doderovic they took us out one by one to be interrogated by Popic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Where was Popic's office?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Popic's office was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were you interrogated there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was interrogated and beaten upstairs. They brought me some -- some paper to sign, but I didn't want to, and I was bloody all over.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Do you recall who beat you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Slobo Todorovic, Vlatko Doderovic and Bosko Starovic beat me. They tied me to a chair and beat me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And what kind of questions were they asking you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They were only saying, Alija doesn't want you. But they -- these were mostly the words they used. Now be happy with Alija; Alija doesn't want you, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were you beaten on one occasion or -- or more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I was beaten several times. But that's when they beat me worse, when I didn't want to sign. And I saw that they were stating some untruths that I had killed, I don't know how many Serbs, and raped, I don't know how many women, and I didn't want to sign that. And that's when they beat me most. But I was taken out five or six times to be beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And during your detention there in the Gacko SJB, did -- were the other members of your cell taken out as well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Did any of the other people in your group, were they interrogated as well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody was interrogated. Everybody was taken out, one by one, beaten up badly, and then the person would be taken to Popic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were you taken to Popic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I said that I was taken to Popic's office. They tied me to a chair there, and they beat me there. Slobo and Vlatko and Bosko Starovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Was Popic present while you were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: He was sitting in his office. The door was open, and I was beaten in the hallway. They were beating me until Predrag Koprivica arrived and said I was -- I -- I'm coming from the hotel, and there's screaming and crying there. The Red Cross is coming, so be careful. Take him to the cell so he can wash because I was all black and blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: During your detention at Gacko at this time, did you ever see the chief, Popovic, there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: No. I saw him only when I escaped, before they shot me. I saw him when he was dumping the dead bodies in the canal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: We'll get to that in a minute, sir. How many days were you detained at the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And did it come about --

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was dark down there all the time, so you don't know if it's day-time or night-time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How did it come about that you left the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: How were you released from the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't released. They put us on a military truck and took us to Kotlina which was in the middle of a field, and we were executed there, and I escaped.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Before you were -- before you were put on a military truck, was somebody interrogated that day?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: On that day, they came -- yes, well, there were interrogations every day. The last one was Smajo's wife, and she said that those two assholes, the Samardzics, had beaten her up, and she heard them saying, "Kill those Turks," and "kick this Bula in the ass," so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Just to clarify, sir, who did she hear saying that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Vitomir Popic, the police commander. He was the Alpha and Omega of everything. The same as Karadzic was in the Republika Srpska, Popic was the same thing in this region.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: All right. You told us that you were put on a military truck from the police station. Could you describe how you left the building and how you were put on the trucks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. They tied us up with strings and drove us on that truck like cattle. And before that, I inquired about Mirko Koprivica, because I knew him, about the whereabouts of some people. And he replied to me, "Dear Asa, whoever came here never saw the light of day again." I don't know where they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Who tied you up with string?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: The two Samardzic brothers and Slobodan Todorovic and the ones that drove us down and executed us. And that police officer from Konjic too.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Was anyone outside the police station as you left?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was, again, this line of women, children, and men beating us with sticks and metal rods. It was the same kind of gauntlet that was there waiting for us when we arrived in the middle of the night, all the way from the truck to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Approximately how long were you in these vehicles, or this vehicle, for before it stopped?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, the distance was about 3 kilometres. First, they drove us around Gacko, and then headed to Kula, and then onto Kotlina over a bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at a document that's in the binder, behind tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 10253. Sorry --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Once again, it's a perspective you will not be familiar with because it is taken from the air. But if could you just have a look at that photograph, sir, and tell us whether you're able to assist us with what it is.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: This is the road toward Kula. To the left there's an Gatacko Polje. And here's the road to -- to Kula. And then you can see Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So am I right in saying that the town at the top of the photo is the town of Gacko?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said. It's Gacko.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And the -- the white road that we see in the centre of the photograph, is that what you're referring to as the road towards Kula?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I meant when I said the road to Kula.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Are you able to see on that photo where the trucks stopped?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I think it's hereabouts. Where there is the brook.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Perhaps the -- perhaps you could mark the photograph, sir, with a number 1 where the truck stopped.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit Number P00920. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] If I may, Your Honour, this is just -- the witness is just explaining to me that what he --

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm not sure whether the Registrar is trying to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honours, the witness is just explaining to me ... different location, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, please keep the microphone close to you because we didn't hear what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I was saying the witness just marked with number 1 which ... the picture. He's just explaining to me the location he was supposed to mark is a bit on the right of what he actually marked so he was saying that he marked the wrong spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Did you hear Judge Harhoff? Please ask him to put a 2 where he wishes to -- in what he regards as the correct spot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] The witness has marked it with a number 2, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, can the -- can the picture be held up at least so we can see where the numbers have been put, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I trust, Mr. O'Sullivan, you can make it out because I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what happened when the vehicle stopped?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: When the vehicle stopped, they chased us out of the trucks and sent us towards the bridge so that when they killed us, we could fall into the river. We all stayed on the bridge. The bodies did not fall until the moment Popovic and the rest of them came and threw the bodies down into the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So who asked you to get out of the trucks?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Professor Dragan Razetic [as interpreted] he was in charge and in command of the shooting. He didn't have a rifle. He only had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Who else was there besides the other members of your group who had come from the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Slobodan Todorovic, the policeman from Konjic, and two Samardzics brothers, Nedjo and Zoran, and there was also Ramo Sudzum, Ramilo. And also Vlatko Doderovic was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: So you were asked to get out of the trucks and then what are you told to do?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: He told to us line up at the end of the bridge by the abutment. And we did. I was looking down. I didn't dare look straight into their eyes. I saw them lined up holding the rifles, the ones I just mentioned. We were standing there, and then he shouted the order, Fire. This professor, Dragan Rasatic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And what happened when he said the words "fire."

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: They fired. A bullet hit me. I fell down, but I was hit in the arm. I looked around. Everybody was lying on the ground. And then two lads Sutko and Ervin started running. They chased them and only Lazetic stayed, and he took a pistol and shot everybody in the head. And then he came to me and herded around and shouted after them, "Chase them, chase them, they're wounded, they can't go long." And then he said that he had only one bullet left in the pistol, and then I decided that it was an opportunity for me to run, because if he fired the shot and missed me I was stronger than him physically. I could fight him, and that's when I decided to run.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: You -- you've told us that you were -- you were wounded at this time. How many --

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the arm and in the stomach. But none of the organs were damaged. I was only slightly wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were you able to see what had happened to the members of your group who were beside you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: As I started running towards Gela Ljut [phoen], everything was flatter, up to the Gela Ljut. There are some other places, Sipovo, Lijeska and other hamlets. I hid there while they were chasing me and running after me, and then when they saw that I had escaped to that place Ljut, they returned. They came there to [indiscernible] lads came and took my -- me to their house from which they had been observing the whole situation. And then Dzevad Dzankovic took binoculars and then he said -- here, you can see that a car -- a Lada came to the scene. I believe that it is a police car. And they saw that the two lads had escaped, maybe 3 kilometres away they were by then. And they saw that the two of them had escaped, that I had escaped, and then they took everybody else and threw them in the water and then they threw a grenade into the water. They sat into the car and returned towards Gacko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Pidwell, this is the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Certainly, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pidwell, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Mr. Basic, before the break, you were telling us of -- of how you had -- of events that took place after the shooting on the bridge. I just want to take you back and ask you a few more details about what happened on the bridge on this day.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I can't hear a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you hear me now? Are you able to hear me through the speakers now?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again, and please let me know if you are able to answer it. I want to take you back to the events on the bridge that day that we were talking about before the break. Are you able to hear me, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] ... give us two minutes ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that you're saying something, but I don't understand a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: You are able to understand me now, sir? Mr. Basic, can you hear my voice?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Can you speak up? I can't really hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Okay. I'll ask the interpreters to speak up maybe. I'll ask another question, and we'll see if that -- if we can progress.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Now I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few more details about what happened on the bridge at Kotlina.

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Okay. Go on, ask me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: You have told us that you were -- that your arms were bound by rope or string but -- when you left the police station. Were they still bound when you were standing on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: When I fell down, then the string broke. After that, my hands were untied.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: Were the other members of your group also bound in the same manner?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, everybody was the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And after you were shot and fell to the ground, were you able to see what happened to the members of your group who were beside you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: I saw them lying on the ground covered in blood, and there was a lot of blood [indiscernible] flowing down the bridge, and people were drenched in blood. There was a lot of a blood and they were all lying. Only the two that I mentioned, the two lads, started running to a different side in the direction of the thermal power plant.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
utterances.text: And you've told us that you stood up -- were able to stand up and start running. Was anyone else besides the two lads able to do that as well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM BASIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. The two lads Sutko and Elvir, they did that and they ran. I don't know about the others whether they were able to do that or not. But they were all seriously wounded. But, you know, let me tell you. Even -- even if they hadn't been shot, they had been so heavily beaten in the prison that they would not have survived any way. For example, Smajo had been so heavily beaten up that if he hadn't died after the shooting, he would have died anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. PIDWELL
